lem-capped-diis-coefficient-minimizer-ex.conclusion: Capped DIIS least squares has a unique minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer, even with singular Gram matrix; no converse characterization of residual matrices is asserted.

lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform.conclusion: A positive occupied gap g and a perturbation of at most g/4 imply cluster separation and the resolvent bound4/g, without a converse perturbation threshold.
lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform.empty: The ordered eigenvalues lambda_r and lambda_{r+1} in the Statement require 1<=r<n, so neither occupied nor virtual cluster is empty.
lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform.endpoints: checked|Proof steps1.1 and2.1 include equality in ||H-H0||<=g/4 and still give distance at least g/4 and gap at least g/2; the contour endpoint parameters0 and2pi describe the same point.

lem-gapped-projector-map-well-defined.conclusion: The strict rth gap implies a unique occupied rank-r projector independently of within-cluster eigenbasis choices; uniqueness is not used to infer a gap.
lem-gapped-projector-map-well-defined.empty: Its Statement uses the occupied projector domain1<=r<n, and proof1.1 selects the first r eigenvectors in an existing finite Hermitian eigenbasis.
lem-gapped-projector-map-well-defined.one: checked|Proof2.1 sums u_j u_j* over1<=j<=r. For r=1 this is the single orthogonal rank-one projector; basis phase changes leave that term unchanged.

lem-projector-is-admissible-density.conclusion: Hermitian idempotence and trace r imply density admissibility; the converse is expressly not the claim.
lem-projector-is-admissible-density.empty: The supplied projector has1<=r<n; its occupied and complementary dimensions are both positive, so the fixed finite eigenvalue list is not empty.

lem-admissible-density-domain-is-closed-.conclusion: The fixed-trace density domain is nonempty, closed, convex and Frobenius complete; these properties are not a characterization of other domains.
lem-admissible-density-domain-is-closed-.empty: checked|Proof1.1 supplies diag(1,...,1,0,...,0) with r ones as a member of D_r, using n>=2 and1<=r<n.
lem-admissible-density-domain-is-closed-.endpoints: checked|Proof4.1 takes every t in[0,1]; at t=0 or1 the convex combination is one of the two supplied admissible densities.

thm-block-projector-frechet-derivative-a.conclusion: A strict occupied/virtual gap yields a C1 block-projector map and derivative estimate16R/g^2; no eigenvalue simplicity within a block is necessary.
thm-block-projector-frechet-derivative-a.empty: The two spectral clusters have dimensions r and n-r with1<=r<n; proof2.1 integrates the full nonempty occupied cluster.
thm-block-projector-frechet-derivative-a.endpoints: The differentiability domain in the Statement is the open perturbation ball||H-H0||<g/4; no derivative at its boundary is asserted. The closed contour has a positive distance from the spectrum by the supplier.

thm-contractive-scf-convergence-and-inex.conclusion: A contraction on a supplied nonempty complete invariant metric space gives fixed-point and residual/error estimates; a small residual alone is not asserted to imply contraction.
thm-contractive-scf-convergence-and-inex.empty: checked|Statement explicitly assumes K nonempty and supplies X0; proof3.1 treats k=0 by the empty convolution sum, equal to zero.
thm-contractive-scf-convergence-and-inex.one: checked|If K has one point, the self-map fixes it and all distances in proof2.1 and2.2 are zero, so the same inequalities hold.
thm-contractive-scf-convergence-and-inex.endpoints: checked|Statement permits q=0 and defines q^0=1. Proof2.2 divides only by1-q>0; q=1 is excluded by the contraction assumption.

lem-density-mixing-preserves-domain-but-.conclusion: A convex mixture of an admissible density and response projector stays admissible, while idempotence may fail; it is not an equivalence with projector membership.
lem-density-mixing-preserves-domain-but-.empty: D and its defined response are supplied in the Statement, so both endpoints of the convex combination exist.
lem-density-mixing-preserves-domain-but-.one: The item concerns two specified matrix endpoints and a scalar mixture parameter, rather than a claim about one-dimensional projector domains; the inherited rank condition is1<=r<n.

thm-gapped-response-projector-lipschitz-.conclusion: A common positive-gap contour and an LF-Lipschitz field yield q=16R LF/g^2, with invariance additionally required for a contraction; gap alone is not sufficient.
thm-gapped-response-projector-lipschitz-.empty: The estimate is quantified over supplied X,Y in K. If K is empty there is no such pair and no fixed-point-existence assertion; its conditional contraction conclusion also requires a self-map.
thm-gapped-response-projector-lipschitz-.one: checked|For a singleton K the only pair has X=Y, so proof1.1 has zero field difference and the contour integral difference is zero.

cor-finite-basis-energy-model-has-c1-res.conclusion: C2 energy data make the Hermitian response C1; at a supplied gapped P0 its occupied projector is locally C1, with no converse regularity claim.
cor-finite-basis-energy-model-has-c1-res.empty: For the local occupied-projector assertion the Statement supplies P0; proof2.1 chooses its gap-preserving neighborhood by continuity rather than a point from an empty model domain.

thm-density-mixing-contracts-under-jacob.conclusion: An invariant relaxed response with an independently certified induced norm q<1 is contractive; positive mixing alpha alone is not a converse certificate.
thm-density-mixing-contracts-under-jacob.empty: checked|Statement requires K nonempty, closed and convex. Proof3.1 uses those assumptions to obtain completeness and a unique fixed point.
thm-density-mixing-contracts-under-jacob.one: checked|If K is a singleton, the segment in proof1.1 is constant and proof2.1 bounds zero distance by zero; invariance fixes its sole density.

thm-certified-diis-error-inheritance.conclusion: Certified candidate tests and baseline response errors propagate the scalar error enclosure; a commutator least-squares residual is not a converse error certificate.
thm-certified-diis-error-inheritance.empty: checked|Proof3.1 starts its recurrence at k=0, where the convolution sum over j<k is empty and the input boundE0 remains.
thm-certified-diis-error-inheritance.endpoints: checked|Statement includes q=0 with q^0=1; proof4.1 explicitly reduces the error recurrence toE_{k+1}<=eta_k. The endpointq=1 is outside the contraction hypotheses.

ex-occupied-projector-discontinuity-at-z.conclusion: The fixed2x2 diagonal family has different one-sided occupied-projector limits; it supplies a discontinuity example, not an equivalence for all gap closures.
ex-occupied-projector-discontinuity-at-z.empty: The Example fixes n=2,r=1 and actual matricesH(t), so neither spectral cluster nor the one-sided families of nonzero real t is empty.
ex-occupied-projector-discontinuity-at-z.endpoints: checked|Proof1.2 treats t=0 directly: both eigenvalues are zero and the lowest rank-one projector is nonunique. Proof2.1 computes the distinct one-sided limits.

ex-self-consistent-projector-two-cycle-w.conclusion: A concrete rank-one2x2 response cycles betweenP0 andP1 despite gap1; this refutes sufficiency of a gap rather than characterizing convergence.
ex-self-consistent-projector-two-cycle-w.empty: Proof1.1 constructs both admissible projectors; proof1.2 computes each unique occupied eigenspace. No unprovided state or empty spectral block is used.
ex-self-consistent-projector-two-cycle-w.endpoints: The Example has the two specified projector iterates and no interval-valued relaxation parameter; proof2.1 alternates these fixed matrices.

ex-affine-contractive-response-and-resid.conclusion: The specified affine scalar response has fixed point1/2 and attains equality in the residual-error bound; it is one worked instance rather than a converse theorem.
ex-affine-contractive-response-and-resid.empty: checked|The Example uses K=[0,1], which contains the fixed point1/2 explicitly found in proof1.1.
ex-affine-contractive-response-and-resid.degenerate: checked|At x=1/2 both the fixed-point error and residual in proof3.1 are zero; division is only by the constant1-1/2, which is positive.

ex-density-mixture-leaves-projector-mani.conclusion: The specified half-mixture is admissible but not idempotent, disproving preservation of the projector manifold; no converse is asserted.
ex-density-mixture-leaves-projector-mani.empty: The Example supplies the two complementary2x2 rank-one projectors; proof2.1 computes their half-mixtureI2/2, an existing admissible density.

ex-diis-singular-gram-fallback.conclusion: Equal nonzero residuals produce a singular2x2 Gram matrix and configured fallback, even though a capped minimum-norm minimizer exists; not every DIIS input is claimed singular.
ex-diis-singular-gram-fallback.empty: The two explicitly supplied residual matrices are equal and nonzero in proof2.1. Proof3.1 exhibits the feasible coefficient pair(1/2,1/2), so no empty history or feasible coefficient set is involved.

ex-additive-eigensolve-tolerance-residua.conclusion: The scalar numerical response shows why the additive1/100 evaluation error belongs in the residual enclosure; it is not a characterization of all eigensolvers.
ex-additive-eigensolve-tolerance-residua.empty: The Example evaluates the existing scalar pointx=0 in[0,1] and the fixed affine map; no empty data or spectral selection is used.
ex-additive-eigensolve-tolerance-residua.endpoints: checked|The chosen inputx=0 is a domain endpoint; proof1.1 evaluates its computed residual24/100 and proof2.1 obtains the exact certified error1/2.
ex-additive-eigensolve-tolerance-residua.degenerate: The calculation has fixed contractionq=1/2, so its residual denominator1-q=1/2 is nonzero. The response evaluation error is fixed positive1/100; no singular spectral problem is claimed.

thm-level-shift-fixed-projector-equivale.conclusion: This item is a true biconditional, but its two directional rows are already separately checked and outside this template subset.
thm-level-shift-fixed-projector-equivale.empty: Statement inherits1<=r<n, so both compressed blocks have positive dimension. The max and min eigenvalues are therefore taken over nonempty finite spectra.
thm-level-shift-fixed-projector-equivale.endpoints: checked|Proof3.1 explicitly excludes equality of the largest occupied and smallest shifted virtual eigenvalues: equality closes the rth gap, so the unique gapped projector is undefined there.

lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.conclusion: Returning primitives and a finite cap imply at mostN updates andN+1 residual tests; this does not characterize convergence or tolerance attainment.
lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.empty: The Statement concerns a supplied admissible initial iterate and returning primitives, not an empty input history; proof1.1 begins at the actual index0.
lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.zero: checked|Proof3.1 explicitly includesN=0: the initial entered index may test once and returns before any update.
lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.one: checked|WithN=1, proof2.1 permits at most one update from index0 to1; proof3.1 returns at index1, giving at most two residual tests.
lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.degenerate: checked|Proof step 2.1 propagates an early gap or eigensolver failure without another pass, and Proof step 3.1 counts only the entered initial segment. Thus singular responses can shorten the work count without invalidating the bound or implying convergence.
lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.endpoints: checked|Proof2.1 allows continuation only fork<N; proof3.1 treats the terminal indexN as a return before an update, including zero cap.
lem-finite-budget-scf-iteration-work.nonempty-choice: The work proof uses the supplied initial point and returning spectrum/response/comparison services; its induction in proof1.1 through3.1 makes no selection of an unspecified minimizer.
